correctness.rationale: The common base Q=b^(mn) yields exactly iid Q-digit laws P=p^(tensor n) and T=t^(tensor m). Under full positive weights expansions are canonical almost surely. P≠T gives disjoint almost-sure frequency limits by the strong law; P=T implies both m- and n-block independence for one word. Coprime boundaries split every internal cut of each repeated block, forcing coordinate independence, and CRT forces identical primitive one-digit marginals. This proves iff compatibility, uniqueness, singularity and full support for all quantified parameters; exact rational checks of five examples and a 64-by-12 rank calculation supplement but do not replace the analytic proof. No hidden numerical, finite-to-infinite or boundary assumption is needed.

value.rationale: A complete natural classification of strictly positive iid distributions for every pair of distinct commensurable integer bases addresses the precise different-base setting posed in arXiv:2309.07366 Question 5.1. The uniquely forced primitive iid digit law is a structural theorem that pins down the entire compatibility locus; the complementary singular measures nonetheless have exactly the same full support. This is mathematically motivated and useful independently of any generalization to unrelated bases, not a mere routine instance of prior fixed-base singularity.
